questions.questionText:
The story beautifully depicts how good values and a high moral standard can direct young hearts 
in the right direction. 
Why was Aram surprised when he first saw Mourad in the morning? 
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage: 
The story “The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse” is a pleasant and interesting one that highlights 
the purity of youthfulness and the strong moral values of the Armenian Garoghlanian tribe. The story 
revolves around the lives of two cousins, Aram and Mourad, who belong to a poor family but are known 
for their honest nature. Early one morning, Aram is amazed to see his cousin Mourad riding a beautiful 
white horse. As the boys could not afford such a horse, Aram suspects that the horse could have been 
ridden without permission, but his excitement to ride the horse makes him forget his suspicion 
momentarily. 
The two boys spend a few days secretly enjoying the rides and feel a deep connection with the animal. 
However, when they meet the horse’s owner, John Byro, and hear his sad story, they feel a sense of guilt. 
Though Byro recognizes his horse, he is too impressed by the tribe’s reputation to accuse the boys. His 
faith in silence is deeply touching for the boys. Finally, Mourad decides to secretly return the horse to its 
proper stable.
options: Because Mourad was leaving the village
Because Mourad was riding a beautiful white horse
Because Mourad had bought a new bicycle
Because Mourad was moving to another town
questions.explanation: The official answer key provided by Staff Selection Commission is Option (B).

The events in Rajamahendravaram in Andhra Pradesh involving the mass poisoning of consumers by 
milk contaminated with ethylene glycol sound a regulatory alarm. As of March 8, the death toll was 11, 
with approximately 20 other people, including infants, hospitalised. Milk is a staple in Indian 
households and contamination by an industrial compound already infamous in India for its lethality 
carries the potential to trigger a crisis of confidence in local, unbranded milk supplies. Children and the 
elderly are most affected by ethylene glycol poisoning due to their higher metabolic sensitivity and 
lower renal reserves, respectively. This could push people towards pasteurised milk from regulated 

 
 
cooperatives such as Amul or Vijaya, which seems desirable, but a large share of milk is also distributed 
in India through small vendors. Food-safety compliance is as much about punishing bad actors as about 
reducing the cost of doing the right thing. In the informal supply chain, cold-chain monitoring and 
hygiene inspections are almost entirely absent, leaving room for contamination. Subsidised testing kits 
and cooperative chilling facilities can thus reduce the risk at small dairies. Regulators may also consider 
safe-harbour provisions that ease penalties for dairy operators who report contamination at their 
facilities; this could also encourage early disclosure, giving authorities time to save lives.
options: Due to their lower renal reserves.
Due to their higher metabolic sensitivity.

Because they lack access to regulated cooperatives.
